# ETH-USD technical report (as of 2026-11-15)

## Data integrity notes
- **Source of truth:** all exact price and indicator figures below come from `get_verified_market_snapshot`. Values I cite for earlier dates, and for VWMA, come from the `get_indicators` and `get_stock_data` series. The snapshot does not independently verify them.
- **Discrepancy:** `get_stock_data` shows a 2026-11-15 close of **1815.93**. The verified snapshot shows **1815.85**. I use the snapshot value and have not tried to reconcile the two.
- **Incomplete bar:** 2026-11-15 is "today" and crypto trades 24/7, so this daily bar may still be forming. The close, RSI, MACD and Bollinger readings could change before the day ends.
- **Not independently verified:** I did not call `macds`, `macdh`, `boll` or `boll_ub` separately. Their values come only from the snapshot.

## Indicators chosen (8) and why
| Indicator | Role |
|---|---|
| close_200_sma | Long-term trend benchmark |
| close_50_sma | Medium-term trend and dynamic resistance |
| close_10_ema | Short-term momentum and the first overhead reference |
| macd (with macds and macdh from the snapshot) | Momentum direction and acceleration |
| rsi | Overbought/oversold condition |
| boll_lb | Volatility-band extreme (the snapshot also gives boll and boll_ub) |
| atr | Volatility for stop and size calibration |
| vwma | Volume-confirmed trend |

These cover trend, momentum, mean-reversion extremes, volatility and volume with little overlap. Price is also stretched against all three moving-average horizons at once.

## Price action summary
- **Latest bar (11/15):** open 1768.77, high 1837.72, low 1714.29, close 1815.85, volume ~17.17B.
- **Recent decline:** the last 30 verified closes run from 2470.77 on 10/21 to 1815.85. Within that, there was a failed spike on 11/4.
  - On 11/4 the high reached 2446.05 and the close was 2422.31.
  - By 11/5 the close was 2234.48, so the spike reversed completely.
  - The closes from 11/8 to 11/14 were 2120.98, 2131.50, 2050.18, 2055.88, 2016.83, 1927.59 and 1769.12. That is a near-uninterrupted lower-close sequence apart from small bounces.
- **11/14 was the largest single-day drop in the recent sequence.** The close of 1769.12 was down from 1927.59, and the low of 1730.70 was below the lower Bollinger band reading of 1870.63 for that date.
- **11/15:** the intraday low of 1714.29 was a new low for the move. The close recovered to 1815.85, a long lower wick with a close slightly above the lower band (1811.29).
- **Volume:** 11/14 (~17.98B) and 11/15 (~17.17B) are heavy relative to the quiet weekend sessions in late October and early November, e.g. 4.36B on 10/31 and 3.89B on 11/7. This is consistent with active liquidation rather than a thin drift lower.
- **Context:** the 11/15 close is below the 8/18 close of 1916.46, the last close before the 8/19 surge (high 2327.70, volume ~29.6B). It is also below the July–August consolidation lows, including the 8/1 low of 1821.49. The 11/15 intraday low of 1714.29 is the first trade below that area in this dataset since early July. The June swing lows (6/5 low 1540.16, 6/6 low 1506.51) are the next lower reference points in the data. I am not claiming any prior bounce or validation at these levels. They are only reference points from the price history.

## Trend structure (moving averages)
| Level | Value | Price vs level |
|---|---|---|
| Close | 1815.85 | n/a |
| 10 EMA | 2001.78 | 185.93 below |
| VWMA | 2097.72 (indicator tool) | ~281.87 below |
| 200 SMA | 2142.44 | 326.59 below |
| Boll middle (20 SMA) | 2162.97 | 347.12 below |
| 50 SMA | 2377.70 | 561.85 below |

- **Price is below every moving average I pulled.** Price closed below the 200 SMA on 11/8 (2120.98 vs ~2154.5) and has stayed below it since.
- **The 10 EMA is falling steadily.** It went from 2490.62 on 10/16 to 2001.78 on 11/15, with no upticks beyond a small bounce on 11/4 (2317.28 vs 2293.93 the day before).
- **The 50 SMA is rolling over.** It fell from 2552.45 on 10/16 to 2377.70, and the decline is accelerating in recent days.
- **The 200 SMA is flat.** It has held in a narrow 2142–2159 range through the whole window, so it is a neutral-to-slightly-declining anchor rather than a trending level.
- **Death cross watch:** the 50 SMA (2377.70) is still above the 200 SMA (2142.44). The gap is 235.26, down from roughly 408 on 10/16 (2552.45 vs 2144.72). If the 50 SMA keeps falling while the 200 SMA stays flat, a death-cross configuration is possible. It has not occurred as of this data, and I make no timing claim.
- **VWMA** has fallen from 2532.24 on 10/16 to 2097.72. Volume-weighted price is below simple price averages, which means the heavy volume has been occurring at lower prices. That confirms the downtrend rather than suggesting a divergence.

## Momentum
- **MACD:** the line is −139.96 and the signal is −102.34. The histogram is −37.63, and the MACD line is below its signal.
  - The MACD line has deepened steadily from −38.57 on 10/16 to −139.96.
  - There was a brief shallowing around 11/4 (−54.31), which did not hold.
  - It is still printing new lows on this window, so there is no bullish MACD crossover or visible flattening.
- **RSI:** 24.66 on 11/15 and 19.80 on 11/14, both well below the 30 oversold threshold. The 11/13 reading was 24.84.
  - RSI has stayed below 50 for the whole window except 11/4 (54.08), which coincided with the failed spike.
  - Readings of 30–40 for most of late October and early November show persistent bearish momentum, not just a one-day shock.
  - RSI is oversold, but in a strong downtrend it can stay oversold. It is not by itself a reversal signal.
  - On 11/15 the intraday low was lower than 11/14's but RSI ticked up, since the close was higher than 11/14's. The data does not show a clean price/RSI divergence over a longer span. I would not call one.

## Volatility and bands
- **Bollinger:** lower band 1811.29, middle 2162.97, upper 2514.65. The close of 1815.85 is only 4.56 above the lower band.
  - On 11/14 the close (1769.12) was below that day's lower band (1870.63).
  - On 11/15 the intraday low of 1714.29 was below the lower band, and the close landed at it.
  - Closes at or below the lower band are consistent with an extended move. In a trending market, price can "walk" the band for several sessions, so this is not a standalone buy signal.
  - The lower band has dropped from 2354.25 on 10/16 to 1811.29, so the band is falling with price. That shows the volatility regime is expanding to the downside.
- **ATR:** 104.40, up from a low of 78.86 on 11/3. Volatility has expanded alongside the decline. As a rough guide, 1× ATR is ~104, 1.5× is ~157 and 2× is ~209. Recent daily ranges (11/14: 1730.70–1933.95; 11/15: 1714.29–1837.72) are above ATR, so ATR is lagging the current realized range.

## Interpretation
1. **Primary read: bearish, with a strong downtrend and heavy sell-off volume.** All moving-average relationships, MACD, the VWMA slope and the persistently sub-50 RSI agree.
2. **Secondary read: short-term stretched.** RSI under 25, a close at the lower Bollinger band and a long lower wick on 11/15 are the conditions under which relief bounces often occur. This dataset does not show that they have worked here, so treat them as conditions, not predictions.
3. **Conflict to weigh:** the stretched-oversold signals argue for caution on fresh shorts at the lows. The trend and momentum signals argue against catching the move early. They have not resolved.

## Conditional levels (reference only, not a recommendation)
- **If a bounce develops,** the first overhead references are the 10 EMA (2001.78), then the VWMA (2097.72) and the 200 SMA (2142.44), which sit close together. The Boll middle (2162.97) is just above them. A bounce into the 2000–2165 area would still be below the declining 50 SMA (2377.70) and would not change the trend by itself.
- **A trend-change confirmation would need:**
  - Closes back above the 10 EMA and then the 200 SMA zone.
  - The MACD histogram turning up (less negative).
  - RSI recovering above 50.
  - None of these is present now.
- **If selling continues,** the 11/15 intraday low of 1714.29 is the nearest reference. The June lows (1540.16 on 6/5, 1506.51 on 6/6) are the next visible price-history reference points.
- **Risk sizing:** with ATR at 104.40 and realized daily ranges above that, stops measured in ATR multiples should be wide, and position sizes should be smaller than at the October volatility level.
- **Watch for the day to close:** whether 11/15 closes above the lower band (1811.29). Today's bar is still open, so the lower-band close and the RSI recovery from 19.80 are provisional.

**Recommendation**: Underweight

**Rationale**: Both analysts agree on the facts: ETH-USD is deeply oversold in a clear downtrend. The question was which reading matters more for positioning right now. The bear wins, but not by enough to justify a full Sell.

The bull has real points. RSI of 19.80, capitulation-scale volume (about 18B vs. a 4B baseline), a long lower wick on 11/15 and a close at the lower band (1811.29) are the conditions where relief bounces often happen. He also defines invalidation clearly at 1714.29. He's right that the Fed headwind is consensus (98% no cuts in 2026) and recession odds are low (2%). He was also candid that this is a tactical bounce idea, not a reversal call.

The bear took apart the parts the bull's trade depends on:
(1) The key bar hasn't closed. The bull concedes this and still builds his case on it. The bar also closed at 1815.85, below the 8/1 support level of 1821.49 that the bull says was reclaimed. That level is now overhead resistance.
(2) The stop is inside normal noise. A stop at 1714.29 is about one ATR (104.40) away, while recent daily ranges were 123-203. The technical report itself says to use wide stops and small sizes. At a 2x ATR stop (about 1607), the first target at the 10 EMA (+10.2%) is below 1:1 reward-to-risk. Using the June lows (1506-1540) as the stop makes it worse.
(3) Retail hasn't capitulated. StockTwits runs about 8 bullish to 1 bearish, with comments like 'adding size, 1770 SL.' That's still a dip-buying crowd, and a cluster of stops just under spot is fuel for a flush.
(4) There's a lot of overhead supply. The 10 EMA, VWMA, 200 SMA and Bollinger midpoint all sit between 2002 and 2163, and the 50 SMA (2377.70) is still falling.
(5) The last relief rally failed. The 11/4 move to 2446 reversed completely, and the 8/19 breakout has been fully erased.
(6) The bull's 'lagging indicators' argument cuts both ways. RSI and the Bollinger bands are built from the same closes, so if lag discounts the moving averages and MACD, it discounts the bull's signals too.

The bear's macro rebuttal (hawkish headlines, the weakness being specific to ETH since growth is fine) is fair, but it relies only on headlines, so I gave it less weight.

Why not Sell: the bear concedes a bounce is plausible. Oversold readings at this extreme raise the risk of a sharp squeeze, so I'd trim rather than exit or short.

Data gaps: we have no ETH-specific news and no on-chain, staking, fee, ETF-flow or FRED data. The 11/15 bar is provisional, and the prediction-market and sentiment samples are thin. Conservative Analyst: First, where we agree: you end up at flat, and so do I. I'm not arguing for buying this, and nothing says a long is safe. Our disagreement is narrower. It's about what the plan authorizes, how much size it allows, and how much you trust the stop.

Any downstream process that reads "Sell" with an entry and a stop can reasonably treat it as a short. The plan's own reasoning says the real action is to stay flat, so the proposal should say that: no trade, hold cash. A short that only exists on a conditional basis shouldn't be pre-authorized by a one-word label.

The 1.2R to the 1714 low is real arithmetic, but a 1.2R target needs roughly a 45% win rate just to break even, before slippage and funding if this is done through derivatives. Fourteen messages over 90 minutes from one source, with low confidence, is too thin to read as contrarian evidence in either direction. The idea that "1770 stops are fuel" is unproven too. Sixth, the gaps cut against shorts more than longs. We have no ETH news, no ETF flows, no on-chain data. Claims about Tom Lee and Saylor buying are unverified, but they're exactly the type of one-directional catalyst that gaps a short against you. The macro read is headlines without figures, and "no cuts in 2026" at 98% is already priced, so it isn't new information.

Also note that 11/15 is a Sunday and the bar is still forming. The next real test is Monday's equity open, when the rest of the book reacts too.

So my adjustment is this. Relabel the decision as hold and stay flat. If a tactical short is ever wanted, make it a confirmed-rejection trade rather than a resting order at 1950. That means price reaches the 2000 to 2100 zone, fails, and closes back under the 10 EMA with the MACD histogram not improving. Cap it at 25% of a unit, size it so dollar risk reflects a stop of at least 2x ATR, and net it against the existing COIN and MSTR shorts. Cut size before widening the stop. The aggressive case treats waiting as lost opportunity, but a trade we skip costs us a missed gain, while a squeeze we're caught in costs us capital.

If price reclaims the 200 SMA zone with MACD turning up and RSI back above 50, the short thesis is off and we reassess. If it breaks 1714 on heavy volume, I wouldn't chase it. I'd wait for a retest. Either way, the small size keeps us in the game for both outcomes.
